title: HybridRobotics/supermimic
why_read: A robotics project tackling whole-body humanoid motion tracking using a single differentiable world model, relevant to current research trends in learned robot control.
analysis: Whole-body motion tracking for humanoid robots is a hard control problem because it involves coordinating many joints and maintaining balance while matching reference motions. Using a differentiable world model suggests the system can be trained end-to-end with gradients flowing through a learned simulation of robot dynamics, which is more sample-efficient than typical model-free reinforcement learning. This fits into an active research area combining model-based RL and humanoid robotics, following work like world models in other domains. The project seems to have real adoption given its stars and forks, suggesting it's a usable research codebase rather than just a demo.
